report.summary: Large-scale refactoring verification relies on compilation (Google's ClangMR: 99.9% success over 10,000+ changes, verified by building and testing), static analysis (OpenRewrite uses type resolution; Error Prone embeds proven fixes), AST diffing, and gradual rollout with monitoring. Beyond tests, teams use change impact analysis and community review. No formal proofs are used; semantic preservation is ensured through domain-specific constraints and extensive test suites.
risks: Reliance on test coverage may miss edge cases; static analysis cannot guarantee full semantic preservation.

handoff.suggestion: Integrate differential fuzzing into the refactoring pipeline: automatically generate random inputs for refactored functions, run before/after binaries, and assert behavioral equivalence on a representative code-path sample.
